## R01: Lock order and reentrant calls

**Failure pattern:** one path takes A then B while another takes B then A; or a
helper/callback reacquires a nonrecursive lock its caller already holds. The
second case can deadlock on a single thread. Nested reads also need review when
a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Account archive snapshots, history projections and delivery recovery share the
plaintext-sidecar order: sent, received, then received files. Recovery must not
hold received while waiting for sent: an archive has no delivery guard and can
otherwise hold sent while waiting for received. The real recovery regression
`recovery_does_not_hold_received_while_waiting_for_sent` in the
[recovery owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) holds sent,
probes received at the actual acquisition boundary, then releases contention and
joins the worker before asserting replay and progress.
Archive revision snapshots must read and release device-sync policy before
acquiring plaintext sidecars. Attachment commit holds delivery and policy while
checking the live received-file card; an archive holding received files while
waiting for policy creates a cycle and can also block erasure behind delivery.
Keep archive-key revalidation after indexing and page selection so a changed
policy still invalidates the export. The regression belongs to the
[account archive owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/archive.rs)
and must qualify progress while the competing policy/sidecar boundary is held,
then release and join both owners before asserting the outcome.
The same boundary applies to file-proof revisions: identity import holds the
proof store while validating received-file rows. Archive snapshots must read and
release proof metadata before taking sidecars, and retain proof revision in the
final archive-key validation. Its separate held-proof regression qualifies the
actual archive path; policy-only coverage does not establish this lock order.
Do not build a revision array from chained mutex temporaries: guards can survive
until the entire array statement ends. Snapshot each value in a completed
statement before acquiring the next metadata lock. The archive's held-identity
control must also prove suppression is free, preserving the identity-then-
suppression order used by file-row visibility checks.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

Rust [temporary scopes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes)
can keep guards alive through the complete statement, including struct literals
## R06: Exact authority and stale completions

When projecting account roles into device-shaped display fields, derive the
representative from the current validated account membership. A historical
legacy device owner cannot describe a transferred account role. Keep exact
account/device validation and bounded-snapshot inclusion together at the
[inventory publisher](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/inventory.rs);
the real modern and legacy transfer regressions in
[owner target tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/owner_targets.rs)
check readable inventory while preserving grants and the legacy owner field.

**Failure pattern:** work authorized before an await or queue delay commits after
logout, same-user relogin, account replacement or a policy off/on transition.
Comparing only the username or current Boolean value misses changed authority.

Capture the owner's exact session/runtime installation and relevant revision at
entry. Revalidate through the existing atomic commit seam before side effects
and before publishing private results. Treat frontend generation guards as UI
ownership, not host authorization. Read commands can expose stale private data too.
When consolidating repeated database reads, keep reuse inside the current
synchronous connection owner. Preserve identity/generation error precedence and
retirement-job integrity before reading capability metadata, and repeat live
session/deadline validation at its final owner. The repository network validator's
[regressions](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/eventlog/repository/network/tests.rs)
count executed scope reads and retain stale-view, corruption and capability-change
controls; a prepared-statement compilation count does not measure executed reads.
Bind session effects to exact owner/generation rather than a replaceable display
object. Cosmetic profile refreshes must not restart inactivity timers, republish
call state or count as user input. The mounted [App regressions](../frontend/src/App.test.ts)
exercise metadata updates, actual input and same-owner session replacement.

A closing popup's delayed cleanup can outlive a newer popup's focus ownership.
Default restoration may act only while focus is neutral or still belongs to the
closing content. Reuse the [shared focus owner](module-boundaries.md#dialog-focus-ownership)
## R08: Durable state and failure semantics

Before replacing an installed application, fetch and compare the intended source
base with the current integration branch and inspect persisted schema compatibility.
A locally successful build can still downgrade an installed reader. Never delete
or recreate a newer database to make an older reader start. The
[pack storage owner](../frontend/src/store/packs.ts) and its
[storage regressions](../frontend/src/store/packs.test.ts) own catalog migration;
verify installed appearance and retained library contents after replacement,
not only a clean-profile startup. Keep source freshness and schema compatibility
as separate evidence from signature validity and notification authorization.

**Failure pattern:** a read-modify-write race loses another update; optimistic
success precedes durable acceptance; retries duplicate writes; a failed/corrupt
read is silently treated as empty state; cleanup after a partial failure destroys
recoverable user data.

Identify the commit point, serialization owner and restart/replay behavior.
Prepare expensive work separately, then compare expected revision and lifetime
under the owning commit guard. Preserve operation IDs, ordering, atomic replacement
and existing compatibility rules. Multi-store changes are not automatically one
transaction; define recovery or compensation for every partial commit boundary.
Use established error types and distinguish absent, unavailable and corrupt data.

Retire successfully handled controls from derived receive work, including controls
encoded as ordinary Message events. Define recovery across effect and scheduling
commits before discarding the effect's authentication inputs. A terminal no-op
classification may retire only work that a matching durable, monotone state can
never require again; it must not grant authority or manufacture success. The
[receipt owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) and
`authenticated_receipt_retirement` regressions cover quiet replay, failed marker
persistence after delivery, restart without the original body, current ownership
and ordinary-message isolation. See the [state contract](network-design-reference.md#state-and-concurrency-contract).

Separate authoritative durability from disposable SQL query progress. The
[selection owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/eventlog/repository/selection.rs)
uses the existing connection's encrypted temporary pager for derived ranks and
cursors; reopening rebuilds them from current MAIN records. Failed preparation
`ui/lib/recoveryRefresh.ts` owns coalesced foreground activation and sparse
five-minute fallback for presentation/account projections. Native invalidations
and accepted local edits remain prompt. Pure presentation can park fallback while
hidden; durable publication retries remain owned in the background. Modern hosts
avoid short polling; presence/file legacy compatibility retains its explicit
cadence. Calls and network receive keep their own owners and deadlines.
`ui/store/chatExpiry.ts` schedules the next actual loaded-message, receipt-ledger,
file or search-context expiry with a monotonic floor and a sparse clock check
only while expiring content exists. Quiet state publishes no clock tick. Chat
boot/group controls retain a timer only while recovery or an operation is pending.
`conversationState.ts` evicts inactive presentation arrays under the existing
50-conversation cap and an 8 MiB charged-payload budget. The active page, durable
reception/deletion evidence and pending send intents retain their existing owners;
this budget is not a total renderer-residency ceiling.

`core/eventlog/repository/` owns physical event counts and record-cost estimates,
including their append and removal updates, conversation retirement authority,
and bounded graph reclamation. Its admission gate preserves validation and
counter errors before reserving new growth or allocating a stored-event encoding.
`core/postoffice/storage/` owns relay first-arrival time, touch, role readiness,
monotonic expiry visibility, capacity backpressure and persistent drain work on
the same profile connection. Relay transactions reuse repository admission and
physical charge rather than maintaining parallel counters. Indexed role pending
state changes with repository retirement, and matching arrival removal shares
its finalization transaction. Policy-bearing reads qualify current eligibility;
physical diagnostics alone cannot qualify custody. Runtime and paced worker
adoption remain separate. See [storage ownership and budgets](ARCHITECTURE.md#storage-replay-and-query-budgets).

`core/storage/profile/participant.rs` owns participant control metadata, explicit
source locators and recoverable account-adoption intent on the shared connection.
Its `participant/event_ownership.rs` owner commits account-qualified event ordinal
ranges and a monotonic captured-owner generation with adoption; receive schedulers
derive indexed namespace selectors from those exact ranges rather than inferring
ownership from conversation IDs or replacing an older account's pending work.
`core/node/delivery_runtime.rs` remains the account-adoption decision owner and
coordinates its existing delivery journal with that intent.
`core/storage/profile/participant_events.rs` owns independent event-source
publication, its downgrade barrier, authenticated import and retryable cleanup.
`core/eventlog/persist.rs` selects the profile-backed repository for production
Nodes; `persist/legacy.rs` retains the explicit standalone compatibility owner.
`core/identity/device.rs` owns immutable private device keys and one fixed public
projection per identity. Creation and keystore restoration derive that projection
once; callers receive an owned clone. Public reads add no retained state and do
not cache signature validity, membership or permissions.

`core/node/account_devices.rs` owns the bounded roster of immutable account/device
new signed controls resume after account adoption rather than draining in open.
Fresh authority and recall-readiness checks remain separate from display state.
Installing an indexed current state preserves its exact device-local acceptance
cutoff and the corresponding retry ticket without changing current-epoch sender
retention or indexed receiver retirement. A fresh invitation clears the former
cutoff, and obsolete sender epochs retain their existing retirement policy.
Pure authority projection retains its separate, nonlocal meaning.
The checkpoint cleanup owner retires disposable facts in bounded turns after
logical channel retirement, even when no later read revisits the channel.
Consumed receiver/evidence/receipt state is preserved.
`join_history/indexed/continuation.rs` suspends the existing offer, first-valid
selection, lifetime and release checks at selected database/authority operations.
Each normal retry advances measured operations through the shared owner, causal
or ancestry query APIs within one shared row, edge and byte allowance. A finite
command cap bounds phase-only work. A selected allocation that cannot fit the
remaining allowance retains its command for a fresh turn, with conservative
charging when the admission error cannot report spent work. A command that cannot
fit the caller's full allowance remains an explicit budget error. The existing
recovery loop resumes pending work; no task, connection lock or plaintext queue is
retained between turns. Active receive and
send stacks are capped by the existing retry limits and keep only protocol-capped
encrypted snapshots and current membership. The durable release cursor advances
only with the existing transcript/effect transaction; restart resumes its same
uncommitted candidate. Completed unchanged sender work uses its scalar control
stamp. Explicit local invitation creation still performs synchronous causal checks
for its at-most-ten selected snapshot rows before the journal transaction; it is
not covered by the normal retry latency bound. Directory preparation is a separate
consumer boundary. Other participant domains retain their
legacy owners until their own cutovers. `core/node/runtime_startup.rs` composes
startup inputs and completion through `runtime_work.rs`; blocking captures and
undelivered results remain admitted until their resources are destroyed.
The same runtime owner keeps one separate fair capacity slot for top-level
Readiness and completion must name the operation, source generation and owning
scope being observed. A delay, an empty queue, an unchanged counter or the
absence of a stale effect does not prove that its asynchronous consumer finished.
Retain and await the actual task before making authoritative no-effect assertions.
When a browser seam exposes only a transport resolver, pair its integration
scenario with a component test that captures the real handler or effect task;
select both through the owning validation contract. Preserve browser interaction,
current-operation success, native-bridge identity, visual and strict error checks.

Registered IPC fixtures that install a real `NodeRuntime` must take it under the
runtime slot lock, release that lock and await `stop()` before offline persistence
reads, mock-app destruction or temporary-store removal. `Drop` requests
best-effort cancellation; it does not join producers or drain admitted blocking
work. A controlled admitted-work probe retains its real participant permit and
SDK handle through entry, release and join, and rejects cleanup that returns
while that work remains held. Keep business assertions inside owned cleanup:
release held work, await retirement and then propagate the original panic.
Cleanup must also complete when the body fails before its intended mutation.
Do not require a final business value from a cleanup probe. Collect its outcome,
release its gate and await the same retirement future before checking the probe
or propagating an error. An original-failure regression must preserve the exact
panic payload and independently witness retirement; retaining a store and
rethrowing that payload alone does not prove joined cleanup. A registered
graceful host task provides a separate witness: observe actual shutdown entry
while its cleanup remains held, release it, then require completion and the
awaited stop owner. Drop-only cancellation cannot stand in for that sequence.
Retain stores whenever retirement is unverified. A Rust assertion summary alone
cannot certify process success while native connection teardown remains active;
require the complete test process exit status as well.

Favorites navigation, initial App presentation and ConversationView attachment
acquisition follow this paired contract. Hold consumer progress independently of
transport completion, retire its owner, then release and await that exact task.
Verify that the stale effect remains absent after settlement. A replacement task
finishing first cannot stand in for the retired task. Qualify changes with a
temporary guard-bypass control that fails the stale-effect assertion, then restore
the guard. Fake-time advancement can demonstrate why an old elapsed-time sample
was insufficient; it must not become the completion witness.

Process execution follows the same rule: a command leader exiting does not prove
its descendants retired. Shared runners use the validation stage's process owner
rather than creating an independent nested process group. On POSIX, the outer
owner retains termination escalation and resource leases through verified group
retirement, including ignored-stdio descendants and ordinary leader exit.
Leader exit and pipe closure are independent: bound output draining after group
retirement, fail closed on escaped inherited-pipe holders and quarantine leases
without publishing success. Later cancellation must not clear that uncertainty
when the known group retires; preserve the first failure and original exit status.
Nested cancellation notifies that owner. Windows commands join a private native
job at process creation, before the first target instruction, with no breakaway
or inherited job handle. The owning adapter preserves argv, environment, working
directory and byte streams; its private control pipe never reaches target stdin.
Retirement requires an empty job, a signaled retained leader handle and drained
output. The parent accepts only the current invocation's nonce-bound receipt;
helper exit or kill-on-close containment alone cannot certify cleanup.
PID readiness fixtures install their signal handlers, write the complete PID to
a private staging file and atomically rename it to the observed marker. Readers
accept only a positive safe integer PID; opening or truncating a file is not a
startup acknowledgment. A numeric stdout fragment is not a framed identity;
failed publication must retire the actual created child before reporting failure.
A real held-write control must reject an exposed empty
marker and retain its own child handle for cleanup before publication completes.
Ordinary leader exit starts
owned-scope retirement. Retire remaining descendants and verify cleanup before
returning the leader's exit status or releasing resources. This accommodates
compiler auxiliary processes without process-name exceptions or breakaway.
Record forced retirement separately from command status; it never substitutes
for selected test counts, business assertions or complete output evidence.
A Windows job-termination request also closes an empty job; the recorded flag
does not by itself indicate leaked work.
Job retirement, output drain and error recovery share one bounded cleanup budget
inside the parent's missing-receipt backstop. Cancelled or unverifiably retired work
cannot admit another suite, fallback build or transport operation, or create a
successful reusable receipt. Platform evidence must distinguish cancellation from
an incomplete or mismatched test inventory; success still requires every selected
step and its positive test counts.

Keep stdout and stderr distinct through command capture. Cargo JSON, test
inventories and executed-case summaries consume complete stdout; the interleaved
log remains diagnostic output. Both raw channel captures share one byte budget,
and truncation invalidates machine evidence. Preserve original launch,
cancellation and cleanup errors when capture validation also fails. Fixture
program bodies stay static; pass paths, module URLs and configuration as argv or
environment data rather than interpolating serialized values into program text.

a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Account archive snapshots, history projections and delivery recovery share the
plaintext-sidecar order: sent, received, then received files. Recovery must not
hold received while waiting for sent: an archive has no delivery guard and can
otherwise hold sent while waiting for received. The real recovery regression
`recovery_does_not_hold_received_while_waiting_for_sent` in the
[recovery owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) holds sent,
probes received at the actual acquisition boundary, then releases contention and
joins the worker before asserting replay and progress.
Archive revision snapshots must read and release device-sync policy before
acquiring plaintext sidecars. Attachment commit holds delivery and policy while
checking the live received-file card; an archive holding received files while
waiting for policy creates a cycle and can also block erasure behind delivery.
Keep archive-key revalidation after indexing and page selection so a changed
policy still invalidates the export. The regression belongs to the
[account archive owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/archive.rs)
and must qualify progress while the competing policy/sidecar boundary is held,
then release and join both owners before asserting the outcome.
The same boundary applies to file-proof revisions: identity import holds the
proof store while validating received-file rows. Archive snapshots must read and
release proof metadata before taking sidecars, and retain proof revision in the
final archive-key validation. Its separate held-proof regression qualifies the
actual archive path; policy-only coverage does not establish this lock order.
Do not build a revision array from chained mutex temporaries: guards can survive
until the entire array statement ends. Snapshot each value in a completed
statement before acquiring the next metadata lock. The archive's held-identity
control must also prove suppression is free, preserving the identity-then-
suppression order used by file-row visibility checks.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

Rust [temporary scopes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes)
can keep guards alive through the complete statement, including struct literals
## R06: Exact authority and stale completions

When projecting account roles into device-shaped display fields, derive the
representative from the current validated account membership. A historical
legacy device owner cannot describe a transferred account role. Keep exact
account/device validation and bounded-snapshot inclusion together at the
[inventory publisher](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/inventory.rs);
the real modern and legacy transfer regressions in
[owner target tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/owner_targets.rs)
check readable inventory while preserving grants and the legacy owner field.

**Failure pattern:** work authorized before an await or queue delay commits after
logout, same-user relogin, account replacement or a policy off/on transition.
Comparing only the username or current Boolean value misses changed authority.

Capture the owner's exact session/runtime installation and relevant revision at
entry. Revalidate through the existing atomic commit seam before side effects
and before publishing private results. Treat frontend generation guards as UI
ownership, not host authorization. Read commands can expose stale private data too.
When consolidating repeated database reads, keep reuse inside the current
synchronous connection owner. Preserve identity/generation error precedence and
retirement-job integrity before reading capability metadata, and repeat live
session/deadline validation at its final owner. The repository network validator's
[regressions](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/eventlog/repository/network/tests.rs)
count executed scope reads and retain stale-view, corruption and capability-change
controls; a prepared-statement compilation count does not measure executed reads.
Bind session effects to exact owner/generation rather than a replaceable display
object. Cosmetic profile refreshes must not restart inactivity timers, republish
call state or count as user input. The mounted [App regressions](../frontend/src/App.test.ts)
exercise metadata updates, actual input and same-owner session replacement.

A closing popup's delayed cleanup can outlive a newer popup's focus ownership.
Default restoration may act only while focus is neutral or still belongs to the
closing content. Reuse the [shared focus owner](module-boundaries.md#dialog-focus-ownership)
## R08: Durable state and failure semantics

Before replacing an installed application, fetch and compare the intended source
base with the current integration branch and inspect persisted schema compatibility.
A locally successful build can still downgrade an installed reader. Never delete
or recreate a newer database to make an older reader start. The
[pack storage owner](../frontend/src/store/packs.ts) and its
[storage regressions](../frontend/src/store/packs.test.ts) own catalog migration;
verify installed appearance and retained library contents after replacement,
not only a clean-profile startup. Keep source freshness and schema compatibility
as separate evidence from signature validity and notification authorization.

**Failure pattern:** a read-modify-write race loses another update; optimistic
success precedes durable acceptance; retries duplicate writes; a failed/corrupt
read is silently treated as empty state; cleanup after a partial failure destroys
recoverable user data.

Identify the commit point, serialization owner and restart/replay behavior.
Prepare expensive work separately, then compare expected revision and lifetime
under the owning commit guard. Preserve operation IDs, ordering, atomic replacement
and existing compatibility rules. Multi-store changes are not automatically one
transaction; define recovery or compensation for every partial commit boundary.
Use established error types and distinguish absent, unavailable and corrupt data.

Retire successfully handled controls from derived receive work, including controls
encoded as ordinary Message events. Define recovery across effect and scheduling
commits before discarding the effect's authentication inputs. A terminal no-op
classification may retire only work that a matching durable, monotone state can
never require again; it must not grant authority or manufacture success. The
[receipt owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) and
`authenticated_receipt_retirement` regressions cover quiet replay, failed marker
persistence after delivery, restart without the original body, current ownership
and ordinary-message isolation. See the [state contract](network-design-reference.md#state-and-concurrency-contract).

Separate authoritative durability from disposable SQL query progress. The
[selection owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/eventlog/repository/selection.rs)
uses the existing connection's encrypted temporary pager for derived ranks and
cursors; reopening rebuilds them from current MAIN records. Failed preparation
`ui/lib/recoveryRefresh.ts` owns coalesced foreground activation and sparse
five-minute fallback for presentation/account projections. Native invalidations
and accepted local edits remain prompt. Pure presentation can park fallback while
hidden; durable publication retries remain owned in the background. Modern hosts
avoid short polling; presence/file legacy compatibility retains its explicit
cadence. Calls and network receive keep their own owners and deadlines.
`ui/store/chatExpiry.ts` schedules the next actual loaded-message, receipt-ledger,
file or search-context expiry with a monotonic floor and a sparse clock check
only while expiring content exists. Quiet state publishes no clock tick. Chat
boot/group controls retain a timer only while recovery or an operation is pending.
`conversationState.ts` evicts inactive presentation arrays under the existing
50-conversation cap and an 8 MiB charged-payload budget. The active page, durable
reception/deletion evidence and pending send intents retain their existing owners;
this budget is not a total renderer-residency ceiling.

`core/eventlog/repository/` owns physical event counts and record-cost estimates,
including their append and removal updates, conversation retirement authority,
and bounded graph reclamation. Its admission gate preserves validation and
counter errors before reserving new growth or allocating a stored-event encoding.
`core/postoffice/storage/` owns relay first-arrival time, touch, role readiness,
monotonic expiry visibility, capacity backpressure and persistent drain work on
the same profile connection. Relay transactions reuse repository admission and
physical charge rather than maintaining parallel counters. Indexed role pending
state changes with repository retirement, and matching arrival removal shares
its finalization transaction. Policy-bearing reads qualify current eligibility;
physical diagnostics alone cannot qualify custody. Runtime and paced worker
adoption remain separate. See [storage ownership and budgets](ARCHITECTURE.md#storage-replay-and-query-budgets).

`core/storage/profile/participant.rs` owns participant control metadata, explicit
source locators and recoverable account-adoption intent on the shared connection.
Its `participant/event_ownership.rs` owner commits account-qualified event ordinal
ranges and a monotonic captured-owner generation with adoption; receive schedulers
derive indexed namespace selectors from those exact ranges rather than inferring
ownership from conversation IDs or replacing an older account's pending work.
`core/node/delivery_runtime.rs` remains the account-adoption decision owner and
coordinates its existing delivery journal with that intent.
`core/storage/profile/participant_events.rs` owns independent event-source
publication, its downgrade barrier, authenticated import and retryable cleanup.
`core/eventlog/persist.rs` selects the profile-backed repository for production
Nodes; `persist/legacy.rs` retains the explicit standalone compatibility owner.
`core/identity/device.rs` owns immutable private device keys and one fixed public
projection per identity. Creation and keystore restoration derive that projection
once; callers receive an owned clone. Public reads add no retained state and do
not cache signature validity, membership or permissions.

`core/node/account_devices.rs` owns the bounded roster of immutable account/device
new signed controls resume after account adoption rather than draining in open.
Fresh authority and recall-readiness checks remain separate from display state.
Installing an indexed current state preserves its exact device-local acceptance
cutoff and the corresponding retry ticket without changing current-epoch sender
retention or indexed receiver retirement. A fresh invitation clears the former
cutoff, and obsolete sender epochs retain their existing retirement policy.
Pure authority projection retains its separate, nonlocal meaning.
The checkpoint cleanup owner retires disposable facts in bounded turns after
logical channel retirement, even when no later read revisits the channel.
Consumed receiver/evidence/receipt state is preserved.
`join_history/indexed/continuation.rs` suspends the existing offer, first-valid
selection, lifetime and release checks at selected database/authority operations.
Each normal retry advances measured operations through the shared owner, causal
or ancestry query APIs within one shared row, edge and byte allowance. A finite
command cap bounds phase-only work. A selected allocation that cannot fit the
remaining allowance retains its command for a fresh turn, with conservative
charging when the admission error cannot report spent work. A command that cannot
fit the caller's full allowance remains an explicit budget error. The existing
recovery loop resumes pending work; no task, connection lock or plaintext queue is
retained between turns. Active receive and
send stacks are capped by the existing retry limits and keep only protocol-capped
encrypted snapshots and current membership. The durable release cursor advances
only with the existing transcript/effect transaction; restart resumes its same
uncommitted candidate. Completed unchanged sender work uses its scalar control
stamp. Explicit local invitation creation still performs synchronous causal checks
for its at-most-ten selected snapshot rows before the journal transaction; it is
not covered by the normal retry latency bound. Directory preparation is a separate
consumer boundary. Other participant domains retain their
legacy owners until their own cutovers. `core/node/runtime_startup.rs` composes
startup inputs and completion through `runtime_work.rs`; blocking captures and
undelivered results remain admitted until their resources are destroyed.
The same runtime owner keeps one separate fair capacity slot for top-level
Readiness and completion must name the operation, source generation and owning
scope being observed. A delay, an empty queue, an unchanged counter or the
absence of a stale effect does not prove that its asynchronous consumer finished.
Retain and await the actual task before making authoritative no-effect assertions.
When a browser seam exposes only a transport resolver, pair its integration
scenario with a component test that captures the real handler or effect task;
select both through the owning validation contract. Preserve browser interaction,
current-operation success, native-bridge identity, visual and strict error checks.

Registered IPC fixtures that install a real `NodeRuntime` must take it under the
runtime slot lock, release that lock and await `stop()` before offline persistence
reads, mock-app destruction or temporary-store removal. `Drop` requests
best-effort cancellation; it does not join producers or drain admitted blocking
work. A controlled admitted-work probe retains its real participant permit and
SDK handle through entry, release and join, and rejects cleanup that returns
while that work remains held. Keep business assertions inside owned cleanup:
release held work, await retirement and then propagate the original panic.
Cleanup must also complete when the body fails before its intended mutation.
Do not require a final business value from a cleanup probe. Collect its outcome,
release its gate and await the same retirement future before checking the probe
or propagating an error. An original-failure regression must preserve the exact
panic payload and independently witness retirement; retaining a store and
rethrowing that payload alone does not prove joined cleanup. A registered
graceful host task provides a separate witness: observe actual shutdown entry
while its cleanup remains held, release it, then require completion and the
awaited stop owner. Drop-only cancellation cannot stand in for that sequence.
Retain stores whenever retirement is unverified. A Rust assertion summary alone
cannot certify process success while native connection teardown remains active;
require the complete test process exit status as well.

Favorites navigation, initial App presentation and ConversationView attachment
acquisition follow this paired contract. Hold consumer progress independently of
transport completion, retire its owner, then release and await that exact task.
Verify that the stale effect remains absent after settlement. A replacement task
finishing first cannot stand in for the retired task. Qualify changes with a
temporary guard-bypass control that fails the stale-effect assertion, then restore
the guard. Fake-time advancement can demonstrate why an old elapsed-time sample
was insufficient; it must not become the completion witness.

Process execution follows the same rule: a command leader exiting does not prove
its descendants retired. Shared runners use the validation stage's process owner
rather than creating an independent nested process group. On POSIX, the outer
owner retains termination escalation and resource leases through verified group
retirement, including ignored-stdio descendants and ordinary leader exit.
Leader exit and pipe closure are independent: bound output draining after group
retirement, fail closed on escaped inherited-pipe holders and quarantine leases
without publishing success. Later cancellation must not clear that uncertainty
when the known group retires; preserve the first failure and original exit status.
Nested cancellation notifies that owner. Windows commands join a private native
job at process creation, before the first target instruction, with no breakaway
or inherited job handle. The owning adapter preserves argv, environment, working
directory and byte streams; its private control pipe never reaches target stdin.
Retirement requires an empty job, a signaled retained leader handle and drained
output. The parent accepts only the current invocation's nonce-bound receipt;
helper exit or kill-on-close containment alone cannot certify cleanup.
PID readiness fixtures install their signal handlers, write the complete PID to
a private staging file and atomically rename it to the observed marker. Readers
accept only a positive safe integer PID; opening or truncating a file is not a
startup acknowledgment. A numeric stdout fragment is not a framed identity;
failed publication must retire the actual created child before reporting failure.
A real held-write control must reject an exposed empty
marker and retain its own child handle for cleanup before publication completes.
Ordinary leader exit starts
owned-scope retirement. Retire remaining descendants and verify cleanup before
returning the leader's exit status or releasing resources. This accommodates
compiler auxiliary processes without process-name exceptions or breakaway.
Record forced retirement separately from command status; it never substitutes
for selected test counts, business assertions or complete output evidence.
A Windows job-termination request also closes an empty job; the recorded flag
does not by itself indicate leaked work.
Job retirement, output drain and error recovery share one bounded cleanup budget
inside the parent's missing-receipt backstop. Cancelled or unverifiably retired work
cannot admit another suite, fallback build or transport operation, or create a
successful reusable receipt. Platform evidence must distinguish cancellation from
an incomplete or mismatched test inventory; success still requires every selected
step and its positive test counts.

Keep stdout and stderr distinct through command capture. Cargo JSON, test
inventories and executed-case summaries consume complete stdout; the interleaved
log remains diagnostic output. Both raw channel captures share one byte budget,
and truncation invalidates machine evidence. Preserve original launch,
cancellation and cleanup errors when capture validation also fails. Fixture
program bodies stay static; pass paths, module URLs and configuration as argv or
environment data rather than interpolating serialized values into program text.
